mainTopic: Buying animals from gentiles for קרבנות, why רביעה disqualifies the פרה אדומה, and שילא's source for רבי אליעזר
overview: Earlier, רבי פדת said that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and that the ברייתא allowing people to buy animals from gentiles for קרבנות follows the רבנן. The גמרא suggests that maybe the רבנן allow this only for an expensive פרה אדומה. It rejects that idea with two proofs: the ברייתא would then match no one, and the רבנן quoted a פסוק about all offerings. Next, the גמרא notes that everyone agrees a definite act of רביעה disqualifies the פרה. It tries to prove from this that the פרה is קדשי מזבח. That proof is rejected. First the גמרא suggests the פרה is special because the תורה calls it a חטאת, but that fails because of רבי שמעון's ruling on a יוצא דופן. The final answer is that a מום disqualifies the פרה, and 'corruption' (sexual sin and עבודה זרה) counts as a מום. Then the גמרא examines שילא's source for רבי אליעזר, 'the children of ישראל shall take.' It challenges that reading with רבי אליעזר's own story of buying stones for the אפוד from a gentile, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the רבנן only argued about the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רבנן permit buying from gentiles only for a פרה אדומה, since it is so expensive. For other קרבנות, they would agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Perhaps the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר] only about the פרה אדומה, since its price is very high. But about other קרבנות, they agree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging רבי פדת's claim that the ברייתא about buying animals for קרבנות follows the רבנן. It suggests the רבנן's leniency may be limited to the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה is worth a fortune. So a gentile owner would not risk ruining it through רביעה. Ordinary animals are not that valuable, so maybe the רבנן would forbid buying them for קרבנות, just like רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: [the Rabbis disagree] only about the Red Heifer, since its price is high,
but about other offerings, they agree with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge to רבי פדת's split: the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי פדת's claim that the רבנן allow buying animals from gentiles for all קרבנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The high value of a פרה אדומה may be a special reason for leniency that does not apply to cheaper animals.

steps.title: Then whose view is the ברייתא about buying offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. If the רבנן agreed about ordinary קרבנות, then the ברייתא that permits buying any animal for a קרבן would match neither opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the teaching that 'one may buy an animal from them for an offering': whose view is it? It is neither רבי אליעזר's nor the Rabbis'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 1. It shows that the suggestion leaves a known ברייתא with no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר forbids buying from gentiles even a פרה אדומה, so the ברייתא cannot be his. If the רבנן also forbid ordinary קרבנות, it cannot be theirs either. So the suggestion must be wrong.

phrases.english: But then, that which was taught:
'One may buy an animal from them for an offering,'

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְלָא רַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: whose view is it? Neither Rabbi Eliezer nor the Rabbis!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the רבנן agree with רבי אליעזר about ordinary קרבנות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves the ברייתא permitting any animal for a קרבן with no author.

steps.title: An explicit ברייתא: the רבנן answered with a פסוק about all offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the רבנן answered רבי אליעזר by quoting ישעיהו: the flocks of קדר will be brought up on God's altar. This shows they permit all קרבנות bought from gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it is taught explicitly: What did רבי אליעזר's colleagues answer him? 'All the flocks of קדר shall be gathered to you... they shall come up with favor on My altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger proof against the suggestion of step 1. A ברייתא states openly how the רבנן argued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about animals from קדר, a gentile nation, being offered on the מזבח. That covers regular קרבנות, not just a פרה אדומה. So the רבנן's permission is general, and רבי פדת's split stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The flocks of קדר (a gentile nation)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן permit buying animals from gentiles for all קרבנות, not only for a פרה אדומה. So רבי פדת's split (משנה = רבי אליעזר, ברייתא = רבנן) holds.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught explicitly:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אוֹתִיבוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרוֹהִי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
phrases.english: What did his colleagues answer Rabbi Eliezer?
'All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you...
they shall come up with favor on My altar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of step 1, this time from an explicit source.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן permit gentile animals for all קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording that the רבנן quoted ישעיהו 60:7 against רבי אליעזר

steps.title: The argument is only about suspicion, not a certain case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue only when there is a mere worry of רביעה. If the animal was definitely used for רביעה, everyone agrees the פרה is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about a suspicion. But where he definitely committed bestiality with it, he disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes a new point about the פרה אדומה. It defines exactly where the argument applies. It also sets up the inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת is only about how much to worry when we don't know. A known act of רביעה disqualifies the פרה according to all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to here

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בַּחֲשָׁשָׁא,
phrases.english: They only disagree about a suspicion,
but where he certainly committed bestiality with it, he disqualified it;

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בַּחֲשָׁשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whose view the sources follow to a new point about the פרה אדומה itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A definite act of רביעה disqualifies a פרה אדומה according to everyone. The argument is only about a suspicion.

steps.title: Attempted proof: the פרה אדומה counts as consecrated for the altar
steps.stepSummary: Since רביעה disqualifies the פרה, it must be in the category of קדשי מזבח. Things that belong to בדק הבית are not disqualified by רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the Red Heifer is in the category of items consecrated for the altar. For if it were consecrated for Temple upkeep, would bestiality disqualify it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from step 4 about which kind of הקדש a פרה אדומה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רביעה disqualifies an animal only for the מזבח. Something donated for בדק הבית is not hurt by it. Since everyone agrees רביעה disqualifies the פרה, the פרה must be treated as קדשי מזבח, even though it is not offered on the מזבח itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated for upkeep of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: A definite act of רביעה disqualifies a פרה אדומה. The גמרא first tries to prove from this that the פרה is קדשי מזבח, but steps 6 to 12 reject that proof.
steps.confusionAlert: This 'learn from it' is not the final word. Step 6 pushes back on it, and step 10 explains the disqualification in a way that does not make the פרה into קדשי מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּפָרָה קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הִיא,
phrases.english: learn from it that the Red Heifer is altar-consecrated,
for if it were consecrated for Temple upkeep,
would bestiality disqualify it?!
phrases.notes: The question means 'of course not': רביעה does not disqualify things given for Temple upkeep.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּפָרָה קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the rule in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed inference: the פרה אדומה is קדשי מזבח, since רביעה disqualifies it. Step 6 rejects this, and step 10 explains the disqualification as a kind of מום instead.

steps.title: The פרה is special because the תורה calls it a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 5. רביעה can disqualify the פרה even though it belongs to בדק הבית, because the תורה calls it a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פרה אדומה is different, because the תורה called it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the conclusion of step 5. It offers another reason why רביעה disqualifies the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 reasoned: רביעה disqualifies the פרה, so the פרה must be קדשי מזבח. The גמרא answers that the פרה can belong to the category of בדק הבית and still be disqualified, because the תורה gave it the name חטאת. That name brings along the rules of a חטאת, including disqualification by רביעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Things set aside for upkeep of the Temple, not for the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פרה stops being בדק הבית. It is saying that the פרה, while in that category, gets one special rule: being disqualified by רביעה.

phrases.english: The red heifer is different,
for the Merciful One called it a sin-offering.
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:9, where the פסוק says about the פרה: חַטָּאת הִוא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 5 by offering another explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that the פרה must be קדשי מזבח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is another possible reason why רביעה disqualifies the פרה: the תורה calls it a חטאת.

steps.title: Then a caesarean-born heifer should also be disqualified
steps.stepSummary: If the פרה follows the rules of a חטאת, then a פרה born by caesarean section (יוצא דופן) should be disqualified, as it is for any חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the heifer should be disqualified when it was born by caesarean section!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 6. If the פרה follows all the rules of a חטאת, it should also be unfit when it is a יוצא דופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born by caesarean section is not valid as a קרבן. So if the name חטאת makes the פרה follow קרבן rules, a יוצא דופן פרה should be unfit. This step sets up the problem that step 8 sharpens with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (an attack that follows the logic through)
An animal born by caesarean section, through the side

phrases.english: But if so,
let it be disqualified when born by caesarean section!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of step 6 by following it to an unwanted result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרה follows the rules of a חטאת because the תורה calls it that.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the name חטאת brings קרבן rules, then the rule that a יוצא דופן is unfit should apply to the פרה too.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון allows a caesarean-born heifer
steps.stepSummary: One might simply accept that a יוצא דופן פרה is unfit. But a ברייתא records that רבי שמעון rules it fit, so the 'חטאת' reason cannot work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that yes, it really is disqualified, then why was it taught: If one consecrated it when it was born by caesarean section, it is disqualified, but רבי שמעון declares it fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an easy way out. Someone might say the פרה really is unfit when it is a יוצא דופן. The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא does disqualify a יוצא דופן פרה. רבי שמעון disagrees and calls it fit. So according to רבי שמעון, the פרה does not follow every rule of a חטאת, and the explanation of step 6 fails for him.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say that indeed it is so
Why then was it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: And if you say, indeed it is so,
why was it taught:
If he consecrated it when it was born by caesarean section, it is disqualified,
phrases.notes: "It" here is a פרה being set aside to be the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon declares it fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 7 by closing off a possible answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that a יוצא דופן פרה really is disqualified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון allows a יוצא דופן פרה, so according to him the פרה does not follow all the rules of a חטאת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's general view on caesarean births does not explain it
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי שמעון allows the פרה only because he thinks a caesarean-born animal is a normal offspring. But רבי יוחנן says רבי שמעון agrees that for קדשים such an animal is not holy, so that answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, since he says a caesarean-born child counts as a full, normal offspring, that does not work: didn't רבי יוחנן say that רבי שמעון agreed, regarding sacrifices, that such an animal is not consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the 'חטאת' explanation by tying רבי שמעון's ruling to his general view about caesarean births. It then rejects that attempt with a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that רבי שמעון treats a יוצא דופן as normal everywhere, so a יוצא דופן חטאת would also be fine for him. רבי יוחנן says that in the area of קדשים, רבי שמעון agrees a יוצא דופן is unfit. So if the פרה were treated like a חטאת, רבי שמעון should disqualify it. Since he allows it, the 'חטאת' reason of step 6 is shown to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning from elsewhere

phrases.english: And if you say that Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא,
phrases.english: for he says: one born by caesarean section is a full-fledged offspring,
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Rabbi Shimon would agree
regarding sacrifices that it is not consecrated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense of step 6 and knocks it down, which finishes off the 'חטאת' explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי שמעון's ruling comes from his general view about caesarean births.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן says that for קדשים, רבי שמעון agrees a יוצא דופן is not holy.

steps.title: A blemish disqualifies the heifer, and sexual sin counts as a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The new answer: a מום disqualifies the פרה. A פסוק and the school of רבי ישמעאל teach that 'corruption' (sexual sin and עבודה זרה) counts as a מום. So רביעה and עבודה זרה also disqualify the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the red heifer is different: since a blemish disqualifies it, a matter of illicit relations and idol worship also disqualifies it. As it is written: 'because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: wherever the word 'corruption' appears, it means only illicit relations and idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to why רביעה disqualifies the פרה. It replaces the 'חטאת' reason that just failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself says a פרה with a מום is unfit, even though the פרה is בדק הבית. A פסוק links 'corruption' (משחתם) to a מום. רבי ישמעאל's school teaches that 'corruption' means sexual sin and עבודה זרה. So רביעה counts as a kind of מום for the פרה, without making the פרה into a חטאת or into קדשי מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that disqualifies an animal
A matter of forbidden sexual relations, here meaning רביעה
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

steps.whatToRemember: רביעה disqualifies the פרה אדומה not because it is a חטאת or קדשי מזבח. Since a מום disqualifies it, 'corruption' (sexual sin and עבודה זרה) disqualifies it too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This undoes the proof of step 5. The פרה can stay in the category of בדק הבית and still be disqualified by רביעה, so the earlier sugya's reading of the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן does not force it to be קדשי מזבח.

phrases.english: Rather, the red heifer is different:
since a blemish disqualifies it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נָמֵי פּוֹסֵל בָּהּ,
phrases.english: a matter of illicit relations and idol worship also disqualifies it,
phrases.notes: "Illicit relations" here means רביעה. "Idol worship" means the animal was worshipped as an idol.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them,"
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Anywhere that "corruption" is stated,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it refers only to illicit relations and idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, הוֹאִיל וּמוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed 'חטאת' reason of step 6 with a new reason based on מום.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source-based reason (a פסוק plus a teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה is disqualified by רביעה because the תורה calls it a חטאת, or because it is קדשי מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה is disqualified by a מום, and 'corruption' (sexual sin and עבודה זרה) counts as a מום, so רביעה disqualifies it.

steps.title: Verses showing that 'corruption' means sexual sin and idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from two פסוקים that 'corruption' refers to sexual sin and to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sexual sin is called corruption, as it says: 'For all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.' Idol worship is called corruption, as it says: 'Lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved idol.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim from step 10 that 'corruption' means sexual sin and idol worship. It brings one פסוק for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said that 'corruption' counts as a מום. Here the גמרא shows that the same word, 'השחתה', is used in the תורה for both sexual sin (the generation of the flood) and idol worship. This links the two sins to the word that means a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of forbidden sexual relations

phrases.english: A matter of sexual sin, as it is written:
"For all flesh had corrupted"
"its way upon the earth"
And idol worship, as it is written:
"Lest you act corruptly"
"and make for yourselves a carved idol"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for the claim made in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That 'corruption' includes sexual sin and idol worship

steps.title: Sexual sin and idol worship disqualify the פרה
steps.stepSummary: Since a מום disqualifies the פרה, and corruption counts as a מום, sexual sin and idol worship disqualify it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פרה too: since a blemish disqualifies it, sexual sin and idol worship also disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its answer. A פרה that was used for sexual sin or idol worship is not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason does not depend on calling the פרה a חטאת. That is why it avoids the problem with רבי שמעון and יוצא דופן raised in steps 7 to 9. The rule rests only on the fact that a מום disqualifies the פרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that makes an animal unfit

steps.whatToRemember: The פרה is disqualified by רביעה and עבודה זרה because these sins count as a מום, not because the פרה is a חטאת.

phrases.english: And so the red heifer too,
since a blemish disqualifies it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פָּסְלִי בַּהּ.
phrases.english: sexual sin and idol worship disqualify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא פָּרָה נָמֵי, הוֹאִיל וּמוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the proof from step 11 to the פרה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because a מום disqualifies the פרה, sexual sin and idol worship (which count as 'corruption', a kind of מום) disqualify it as well.

steps.title: שילא's reason for רבי אליעזר: only ישראל may supply the פרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שילא's teaching. רבי אליעזר learns from 'the children of ישראל shall take' that a פרה may not come from גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. שילא taught: what is the reason of רבי אליעזר? It says: 'Speak to the children of ישראל that they take.' The children of ישראל take it, and the גוים do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a teaching it quoted briefly earlier and now looks at it closely. It starts with שילא's source for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a פרה אדומה may not be bought from a גוי. שילא reads the פסוק narrowly: since the תורה names 'the children of ישראל' as the ones who take, the פרה must come from Jews and not from גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to look closely at a teaching quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself: שילא teaches:
What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
As it is written: "Speak to the children of Israel"
"that they take"
The children of Israel take it,
and the gentiles do not take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, תָּנֵי שֵׁילָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that goes back to שילא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the פרה must be taken from Jews and not from גוים, based on 'the children of ישראל shall take'.

steps.title: The same words appear about the תרומה for the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שילא. The same phrase is used about donations for the משכן, so by this logic nothing for the מקדש could be taken from גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, about 'Speak to the children of ישראל that they take for Me an offering', would you also say that the children of ישראל take, and the גוים do not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שילא's reading. It points to another פסוק with the exact same wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the children of ישראל shall take' excludes גוים for the פרה, then the same wording about the תרומה for the משכן should exclude גוים there too. That would mean nothing for the מקדש could ever be bought from a גוי, which sounds too extreme.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces a result of your logic that seems hard to accept
Here: a donation for the משכן
So too / is it also so?

phrases.english: But if so:
"Speak to the children of Israel"
"that they take for Me an offering"
phrases.notes: שמות 25:2, about the donations for the משכן.

phrases.english: so too, would the children of Israel take,
and the gentiles not take?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שילא's reading that 'children of ישראל shall take' excludes גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same wording about the משכן donations would then exclude גוים from supplying anything for the מקדש, which seems wrong.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's own story of buying stones for the אפוד from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that גוים really can't supply anything. The גמרא pushes back with a story told by רבי אליעזר himself, in which the חכמים tried to buy stones for the אפוד from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that this is so, didn't רב יהודה say in the name of שמואל: they asked רבי אליעזר, how far must one go in honoring parents? He said: go and see what a certain גוי in Ashkelon did for his father. His name was דמא בן נתינה. Once they wanted to buy stones for the אפוד from him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the answer 'yes, nothing may be taken from גוים'. It starts quoting a story from רבי אליעזר, and the story continues after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the חכמים were willing to buy stones for the אפוד, an item for the מקדש, from a גוי. That suggests רבי אליעזר does not hold that the משכן פסוק excludes גוים. So the reading 'children of ישראל, not גוים' becomes hard to keep for him.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say?: introduces a source that contradicts you
The apron worn by the כהן גדול, set with precious stones

steps.confusionAlert: The story is about honoring parents, but the גמרא quotes it for a side detail: the חכמים tried to buy stones for the אפוד from a גוי.

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed, that is so,
but didn't רב יהודה say that שמואל said:
They asked רבי אליעזר:
How far does honoring father and mother go?
He said to them: Go out and see

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה גּוֹי אֶחָד לְאָבִיו בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן,
phrases.english: what a certain gentile did for his father in Ashkelon,

stones for the ephod

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the possible answer to step 14 that גוים really may not supply anything for the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that גוים may not supply any items for the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's own story shows the חכמים trying to buy stones for the אפוד from a גוי, so items for the מקדש can be taken from גוים.
